few_shot_examples.text: The Amazon rainforest covers approximately 5.5 million square kilometres and is home to around 10 percent of all species on Earth.
few_shot_examples.label: Fact
few_shot_examples.rationale: This sentence presents two quantifiable, verifiable measurements (area in km² and biodiversity percentage). It uses precise numerical data without hedging, subjective evaluation, or first-person stance. Both figures can be independently verified against scientific sources.

few_shot_examples.text: According to the World Health Organization, approximately 2 billion people lack access to safe drinking water.
few_shot_examples.label: Fact
few_shot_examples.rationale: Attributed to a recognised authority (WHO) and backed by a specific statistic. 'According to' is a classic reporting phrase that signals an external, verifiable source rather than personal opinion.

few_shot_examples.text: The human genome contains approximately 3 billion base pairs and encodes around 20,000 protein-coding genes.
few_shot_examples.label: Fact
few_shot_examples.rationale: Contains concrete scientific measurements with no subjective or evaluative language. The information is established scientific consensus documented in peer-reviewed literature.

few_shot_examples.text: Germany reunified on 3 October 1990 after the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989.
few_shot_examples.label: Fact
few_shot_examples.rationale: States a historical event with a precise date. Historical facts can be verified against primary sources and encyclopaedic references. No opinion markers or hedging are present.

few_shot_examples.text: The unemployment rate in the United States fell to 3.4 percent in January 2023, the lowest since 1969.
few_shot_examples.label: Fact
few_shot_examples.rationale: Cites a government-published economic statistic with a specific date and comparative context. Uses objective data rather than personal assessment of the economy's health.

few_shot_examples.text: The Great Barrier Reef stretches over 2,300 kilometres along the coast of Queensland, Australia.
few_shot_examples.label: Fact
few_shot_examples.rationale: Provides a geographic measurement (length and location) that is objectively verifiable. No personal stance, evaluative adjective, or uncertainty marker is present.

few_shot_examples.text: Researchers at MIT developed an algorithm capable of detecting certain cancers from blood samples with 95 percent accuracy.
few_shot_examples.label: Fact
few_shot_examples.rationale: Reports a research finding attributed to a specific institution with a quantified performance metric. Research results are verifiable through the published study.

few_shot_examples.text: The French Revolution began in 1789 and led to the abolition of the monarchy and the rise of Napoleon Bonaparte.
few_shot_examples.label: Fact
few_shot_examples.rationale: Describes historical events with documented dates and consequences. Both the start year and the political outcomes are part of the established historical record.

few_shot_examples.text: I believe the government's handling of the economic crisis was nothing short of catastrophic.
few_shot_examples.label: Opinion
few_shot_examples.rationale: Opens with 'I believe', a classic first-person epistemic marker. The superlative evaluation ('nothing short of catastrophic') is inherently subjective and emotive rather than data-backed. The same policy could be judged very differently by another observer.

few_shot_examples.text: In my view, electric vehicles are far superior to traditional combustion engine cars in every meaningful way.
few_shot_examples.label: Opinion
few_shot_examples.rationale: 'In my view' immediately signals a personal perspective. 'Far superior … in every meaningful way' is an absolute evaluative claim that cannot be uniformly verified — it depends on criteria chosen by the author.

few_shot_examples.text: This new regulation seems like an overreach that will likely stifle innovation and damage the economy.
few_shot_examples.label: Opinion
few_shot_examples.rationale: 'Seems like' and 'will likely' are hedging expressions indicating prediction rather than established fact. 'Overreach' is a subjective political judgement, and the economic impact is speculative.

few_shot_examples.text: Social media has arguably done more to divide society than to connect it.
few_shot_examples.label: Opinion
few_shot_examples.rationale: 'Arguably' is a classic hedge that signals the author's awareness that their claim is contestable. The comparison is a value judgement that depends on how 'divide' and 'connect' are measured and weighted.

few_shot_examples.text: The film is a stunning visual achievement, though its narrative is disappointingly shallow.
few_shot_examples.label: Opinion
few_shot_examples.rationale: Evaluative adjectives ('stunning', 'disappointingly shallow') represent aesthetic judgements that vary between critics. Such assessments are inherently subjective and cannot be objectively verified.

few_shot_examples.text: Perhaps the most troubling aspect of modern politics is the apparent decline in civil discourse.
few_shot_examples.label: Opinion
few_shot_examples.rationale: 'Perhaps' signals uncertainty and subjective interpretation. 'Most troubling' is an evaluative superlative. 'Apparent decline' combines a hedging word with a value-loaded description that different people may assess very differently.

few_shot_examples.text: The city should invest heavily in green infrastructure rather than continuing to subsidise fossil fuels.
few_shot_examples.label: Opinion
few_shot_examples.rationale: The modal 'should' expresses a normative prescription — the author's view of what ought to be done — rather than reporting what is the case. Policy recommendations are inherently opinion-based.

few_shot_examples.text: Many experts believe the central bank made a serious error by raising interest rates so aggressively.
few_shot_examples.label: Opinion
few_shot_examples.rationale: Even attributed to 'many experts', the core claim ('serious error') is an evaluative judgement. 'Believe' signals subjective assessment. Other equally qualified experts hold the opposite view.
